messages.content: Write a short announcement for a new feature in a note-taking app: offline sync. Around 200 words.

# Offline sync

Your notes now write to the device first and go up to the server whenever a connection is available.

Until now, opening the app without a network gave you a read-only view and a banner telling you to try again later. You could read old notes. You could not change them. This was the most common complaint we got, by a wide margin, from people who write on planes and trains.

Every note now lives in a local database on your device. Typing lands there straight away, with no round trip. When the app sees a connection, it pushes what changed and pulls in anything your other devices wrote while you were away. The status line at the bottom tells you when the last sync finished, and how many notes are still waiting.

Editing the same note on two offline devices produces a conflict. We do not pick a winner. Both versions are kept, and the note opens with them side by side so you can merge them yourself.

Offline sync is on by default in version 3.4, on iOS, Android and desktop. The web app follows next month, once we finish testing storage limits in Safari.
